patterns.what_worked: Each filing named its live consumer, so each change was pinned against the CONSUMER rather than against a copy of it: the CoE widget against classes/shaman.lua's HUD_SLOTS descriptor + the provider's hud_show_<key> == true gate (options_load_state.lua 26, new), the Flame Shock fallback against the shipped default 0 (shaman_state.lua 40, new), the Wolfshead read against the real compat probe through the sandbox's own query counter (druid_state.lua 38). The 1 s throttle with a documented freshness contract kept the tri-state intact and the no-rule-consumes-it pins green without touching druid_guide.lua. The mutation proofs (5/5 killed, control green) are what prove the hot read is really gone rather than merely moved.
patterns.what_was_hard: The dispatch's file list could not be held exactly: the Flame Shock fallback change makes an out-of-scope pin false, because that pin ASSERTED the old 3 s fallback and cited the line the dispatch ordered changed. The minimum mechanical re-cut is the HU-10 precedent, but the boundary is the operator's to rule, not the lane's.
patterns.skill_gap: The druid throttle could have been written as 'skip the read until a rule consumes it' - cheaper still - but that would have made the published input permanently nil and retired the existing tri-state pins for a value nothing reads. Throttling keeps the plug-in point observable; a future lane that lands the SHIFT rule must decide whether the 1 s freshness is enough for it.
